#   - the modern Qt6 GUI (src/CapabilityChecker.cpp; embedded at build time
#   - the legacy Qt3 GUI (legacy/gui/src/LegacyMainWindow.cpp; staged into
# The column's rule is shared: the PROBE-DERIVED package (the helper's proven
# installable side-channel, e.g. display-installable) wins when one exists for
# the row's state; otherwise the static row below names the package(s) that
# provide the capability (the packages that WOULD enable the functionality on
# that distribution family, even when they are not installable there).  The
# Debian-family rows are the legacy capabilitySpecs package values verbatim
# (the parity contract locks the two sources).  A row change is a deliberate,
# reviewed edit: legacy/tests/test-ui-parity-qt3.sh locks the row set and a
# golden checksum, so a one-sided edit fails the gate.
#   key       the capability key (the `Repair tool <key>` vocabulary plus the
#   family    the distribution family: debian, fedora, rhel, arch, alpine,
#             suse, or "*" for every family.  The exact family row wins; "*"
#             is the fallback; a key with no row (or an empty packages cell)
#             has no static package set — the Packages cell then shows only
#             the probe-derived suggestion, or stays empty.
#   packages  the space-separated package name(s).  Raw package names, never
